Fortin et al. (2009) DBH–height model for 20 Québec tree species

Source: R/hd_fortin2009.R
hd_fortin2009.Rd

Vectorized implementation of the population-level height–diameter relationship of Fortin, Bernier, Saucier & Labbé (2009; Mémoire de recherche forestière no 153) for 20 commercial tree species of Québec. Predicts total tree height (m) from DBH (cm), plot basal area, the tree's social status, mean annual temperature, drainage, ecological region and recent light disturbance. All species use the same predictors. The newer hd_auger2016() is the updated relation from the same Québec inventory (27 species).

Usage

hd_fortin2009(
  DBH,
  species,
  BA,
  QMD,
  ecoregion,
  drainage,
  MAT,
  disturbance,
  keep_model_id = FALSE
)

Arguments

DBH

Numeric vector. Tree level. Diameter at breast height (1.3 m), in cm (source "dhp"). Must be >= 0.

species

Character vector. Tree level. NFI species codes (e.g. "PICE.MAR"; compact "PICEMAR" is accepted). Supported: ABIE.BAL, ACER.RUB, ACER.SAH, BETU.ALL, BETU.PAP, FAGU.GRA, FRAX.NIG, LARI.LAR, OSTR.VIR, PICE.GLA, PICE.MAR, PICE.RUB, PINU.BAN, PINU.STR, POPU.GRA, POPU.TRE, QUER.RUB, THUJ.OCC, TILI.AME, TSUG.CAN.

BA

Numeric vector. Plot level. Basal area of all trees with DBH \(\ge\) 9.1 cm in the plot (m²/ha; source "ST"). Must be >= 0.

QMD

Numeric vector. Plot level. Quadratic mean DBH of the plot's trees with DBH \(\ge\) 9.1 cm (cm; source "dmq"), used in the social status index (DBH - QMD)^2. Must be > 0.

ecoregion

Character vector. Plot level. Québec ecological region code (« région écologique », Saucier et al. 1998), e.g. "3a" or "6h"; case-insensitive. Mapped to the four ecological subdivisions of the source (see Details).

drainage

Character vector. Plot level. Drainage class (source "d"): "xeric", "mesic", "subhydric" or "hydric"; French "xérique", "mésique", "subhydrique", "hydrique" (with or without accents) are accepted. CFSForestTools derives it from the physical environment (« milieu physique ») of the ecological type: 0 = xeric, 1–3 = mesic, 4–6 = subhydric, 7–9 = hydric.

MAT

Numeric vector. Plot level. Mean annual temperature, 1971–2000 normal (°C; source "T", from BioSIM).

disturbance

Character vector. Plot level. Light disturbance since the previous measurement (source "f"; partial cut or natural disturbance such as partial windthrow or light insect outbreak): "anthropique" ("anthropogenic"), "naturelle" ("natural") or "aucune" ("none").

keep_model_id

Logical. If TRUE, add column model_id ("fortin2009").

Value

A tibble with column height (m), plus model_id if keep_model_id = TRUE.

Details

Model form (equations 6 and 7, p. 7): $$h = 1.3 + A \ln(DBH + 1) + B \ln(DBH + 1)^2,$$ $$A = \beta_{1,s} + \beta_{2,s} BA + \beta_3 MAT + \beta_{4,d} + \beta_{5,e} + \beta_{6,f} + \beta_7 ISS,$$ $$B = \beta_{8,s} + \beta_{9,s} BA + \beta_{10} ISS,$$ $$ISS = (DBH - QMD)^2,$$ where \(s\) is the species, \(d\) the drainage class, \(e\) the ecological subdivision and \(f\) the disturbance class. Source symbols map to arguments as: ST = BA, dmq = QMD, T = MAT, ISS (« indice de statut social ») is computed from DBH and QMD. Height is not transformed, so no back-transformation applies.

Population-level prediction: the fixed effects with the plot random effect and residual error set to zero, as in the source's validation (eq. 9, p. 8). Plot calibration with measured heights (the source publishes the variance components) is not implemented.

Coefficients: full-precision estimates from the CFSForestTools implementation of this model (fortin2009generalhdrelationship, 0_HDRelationBeta.csv; LGPL-3). They are the same fit as Tableaux 4 and 5 (pp. 11–12) and agree with the printed values to the printed precision (largest difference 5e-5). Predictions match CFSForestTools to within 1e-8 m.

Ecological subdivision: the source groups Québec ecological regions (Saucier et al. 1998) into four subdivisions, shown only as a map (Figure 2, p. 8). As in CFSForestTools, ecoregion takes the ecological region code and is mapped as follows:

  • Ouest (West): 1a, 2a, 3a, 3b, 4a, 4b, 4c, 5a, 5b, 5c, 5d, 6a–6g.

  • Centre: 2b, 2c, 3c, 3d, 4d, 4e, 4f, 5e, 5f.

  • Nord-Est (Northeast): 6h–6l, 6n–6s, 7a, 7b, 7c.

  • Sud-Est (Southeast): 4g, 4h, 5g, 5h, 5i, 5j, 6m.

Figure 5: the effect plots on p. 13 are reproduced within about 0.05 m, except panel (e) (social status index). For a tree 10 cm larger or smaller than QMD, the published coefficients give about 13.2 m while the figure shows about 12.7 m. This function follows the coefficients (as CFSForestTools does).

Applicability: fitted to merchantable trees (DBH \(\ge\) 9.1 cm) of the Québec permanent sample plots, 1970–2006. Trees with DBH < 9.1 cm are computed but reported as outside the range, and their predicted height may be below 1.3 m. Inputs outside the ranges of the fitting data (Tableau 2: per-species DBH; Tableau 1: BA 0.2–66.9 m²/ha, MAT −4.7 to 6.8 °C) are computed and reported in a single warning. Rows with NA in any input return NA height.

References

Fortin, M., Bernier, S., Saucier, J.-P., & Labbé, F. (2009). Une relation hauteur-diamètre tenant compte de l'influence de la station et du climat pour 20 espèces commerciales du Québec. Gouvernement du Québec, ministère des Ressources naturelles et de la Faune, Direction de la recherche forestière. Mémoire de recherche forestière no 153. 22 p.

See also

hd_auger2016(), hd_model_registry(), get_hd_model_info()

Examples

# Reference tree of Figure 5 (balsam fir, Centre subdivision): about 13.4 m
hd_fortin2009(
  DBH = 20, species = "ABIE.BAL", BA = 20, QMD = 20, ecoregion = "4d",
  drainage = "mesic", MAT = 0, disturbance = "none"
)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 1
#>   height
#>    <dbl>
#> 1   13.4

# Inside dplyr::mutate()
trees <- data.frame(
  DBH = c(14, 22, 30),
  species = c("PICE.MAR", "ABIE.BAL", "BETU.ALL"),
  BA = 22, QMD = 18, ecoregion = c("5a", "5a", "3b"),
  drainage = c("subhydrique", "mesique", "mesique"), MAT = c(0.5, 0.5, 3),
  disturbance = "aucune"
)
dplyr::mutate(
  trees,
  hd_fortin2009(DBH, species, BA, QMD, ecoregion, drainage, MAT, disturbance)
)
#>   DBH  species BA QMD ecoregion    drainage MAT disturbance   height
#> 1  14 PICE.MAR 22  18        5a subhydrique 0.5      aucune 12.17414
#> 2  22 ABIE.BAL 22  18        5a     mesique 0.5      aucune 15.47118
#> 3  30 BETU.ALL 22  18        3b     mesique 3.0      aucune 17.88935
